laws.title: Illegal Firearms Possession
laws.subtitle: Owning unregistered or prohibited weapons
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has one of the highest homicide rates in the world, largely driven by gang violence and illegal firearms. The law requires all firearms to be registered and prohibits civilian possession of military-grade weapons. Unregistered firearms are a major driver of violence.
laws.penalty: 3 to 9 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed security companies
Military and police forces

quiz.q: What is the primary driver of Honduras extremely high homicide rate?
quiz.explanation: Gang violence fueled by illegal firearms is the primary driver of Honduras extremely high homicide rate, one of the highest globally.

laws.title: Gang Membership and Operations
laws.subtitle: Joining MS-13, Barrio 18, or other criminal gangs
laws.fullDescription: Honduras is heavily affected by MS-13 and Barrio 18 gang activity, which controls neighborhoods and extorts businesses, bus drivers, and ordinary citizens. Gang membership is criminalized and Honduras has pursued aggressive anti-gang enforcement including mass arrests.
laws.penalty: 9 to 20 years imprisonment; enhanced for leaders
exceptions: None — gang membership is criminal

quiz.q: Which gangs most dominate criminal activity in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: MS-13 and Barrio 18 are the dominant criminal gangs in Honduras, controlling neighborhoods and engaging in extortion, trafficking, and murder.

laws.title: Drug Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Moving cocaine through Honduras toward North America
laws.fullDescription: Honduras is a major cocaine transit country, with significant portions of US-bound cocaine moving through its territory. High-level officials including former President Juan Orlando Hernandez were convicted of drug trafficking. The law imposes severe penalties.
laws.penalty: 15 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed pharmaceutical distribution

quiz.q: What high-profile case demonstrated the scale of drug trafficking in Honduras?
options: Conviction of former President Juan Orlando Hernandez
quiz.explanation: Former Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernandez was convicted in the US for drug trafficking, demonstrating how deeply narcotrafficking had penetrated the highest levels of government.

laws.title: Extortion
laws.subtitle: Demanding payments through threats — war tax
laws.fullDescription: Extortion known as impuesto de guerra (war tax) is pervasive in Honduras. Gangs systematically extort businesses, transport operators, market vendors, and households. Failure to pay results in violence. Honduras has specialized anti-extortion police units.
laws.penalty: 9 to 13 years imprisonment
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What is the local term for gang extortion payments in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Gang extortion in Honduras is called impuesto de guerra (war tax), framing the payment as a tribute owed to the gang controlling the area.

laws.title: Human Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Exploiting people for labor or sex
laws.fullDescription: Honduras is a source, transit, and destination country for human trafficking. Women and children are particularly vulnerable to sexual exploitation and forced labor. The law criminalizes all forms of trafficking with severe penalties.
laws.penalty: 10 to 15 years imprisonment; up to 20 for aggravated cases
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What groups are most vulnerable to trafficking in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Women and children are the most vulnerable groups to human trafficking in Honduras, facing both sexual exploitation and forced labor.

laws.title: Femicide
laws.subtitle: Killing a woman because of her gender
laws.fullDescription: Honduras enacted femicide legislation following alarming rates of gender-based killings. The country has one of the highest femicide rates in Latin America. The law specifically criminalizes killing women in contexts of gender-based power relations.
laws.penalty: 30 years imprisonment
exceptions: None

quiz.q: How does Honduras femicide rate compare regionally?
options: One of the lowest in Latin America
One of the highest in Latin America
quiz.explanation: Honduras has one of the highest femicide rates in Latin America, driving the enactment of specific femicide legislation with severe penalties.

laws.title: Illegal Logging
laws.subtitle: Cutting protected timber without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has lost significant forest cover due to illegal logging, particularly in protected areas and indigenous territories. The law protects forests and imposes penalties on those who cut timber without proper concessions, including in the pine forests of the central highlands.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed timber operations with approved forest management plans

quiz.q: What type of forest is particularly significant in central Honduras?
options: Pine forests of the central highlands
quiz.explanation: Pine forests in the central Honduran highlands are among the most economically and ecologically significant, making their protection from illegal logging crucial.

laws.title: Corruption of Public Officials
laws.subtitle: Bribery and abuse of official position
laws.fullDescription: Corruption permeates Honduran public institutions including police, judiciary, and government. Both paying and receiving bribes is criminalized. Honduras anti-corruption efforts have been hampered by deeply embedded networks of corruption at all levels.
laws.penalty: 6 to 10 years imprisonment; removal from office
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What challenge has hampered anti-corruption efforts in Honduras?
options: Deeply embedded networks of corruption at all levels
quiz.explanation: Deeply embedded corruption networks spanning police, judiciary, and government have made anti-corruption efforts in Honduras extremely challenging.

laws.title: Sexual Violence
laws.subtitle: Rape and sexual assault
laws.fullDescription: Honduras law criminalizes rape and sexual assault with severe penalties. Sexual violence disproportionately affects women and girls and is frequently linked to gang activity. Specialized tribunals handle sexual violence cases.
laws.penalty: 10 to 15 years imprisonment; up to 20 for aggravated cases
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What institutional mechanism handles sexual violence cases in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Honduras established specialized tribunals to handle sexual violence cases with appropriate expertise and victim-centered processes.

laws.title: Drug Cultivation
laws.subtitle: Growing coca or cannabis for drug trade
laws.fullDescription: While Honduras is primarily a transit country, law enforcement has identified cannabis cultivation operations and processing laboratories for cocaine in transit. Growing controlled plants for drug production is seriously criminalized.
laws.penalty: 9 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed research institutions

quiz.q: What is Honduras primary role in the drug trade?
quiz.explanation: Honduras is primarily a cocaine transit country rather than a major production country, though some cultivation and processing occurs within its territory.

laws.title: Wildlife Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Trading in protected animals or their parts
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has significant biodiversity including jaguars, tapirs, scarlet macaws, and sea turtles. Trading in these protected species or their parts violates the Wildlife Conservation Act and international conventions.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed zoos and research facilities

quiz.q: Which marine animal is protected from trafficking on Honduras Caribbean coast?
quiz.explanation: Sharks, sea turtles, and manatees are all protected species on Honduras Caribbean coast, with trafficking in any of them prohibited by law.

laws.title: Illegal Construction
laws.subtitle: Building without permits in protected areas
laws.fullDescription: Honduras planning law requires building permits for significant construction. Building in protected zones — national parks, coastal buffer zones, and indigenous territories — without authorization violates environmental and planning law.
laws.penalty: Fine; demolition order; up to 3 years for protected areas
exceptions: Emergency repairs and minor maintenance

quiz.q: What areas have the strictest construction prohibitions in Honduras?
options: National parks, coastal buffer zones, and indigenous territories
quiz.explanation: National parks, coastal buffer zones, and indigenous territories have the strictest prohibitions on unauthorized construction in Honduras.

laws.title: Kidnapping for Ransom
laws.subtitle: Abducting persons to extort money
laws.fullDescription: Kidnapping has been a significant concern in Honduras, often connected to organized crime networks. Specialized anti-kidnapping units exist within Honduran law enforcement. Both local citizens and foreign businesspeople have been targeted.
laws.penalty: 20 to 30 years imprisonment
exceptions: None

quiz.q: Who are typical kidnapping targets in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Kidnapping in Honduras targets both local citizens and foreign businesspeople, with organized crime networks operating sophisticated kidnapping operations.

laws.title: Child Labor
laws.subtitle: Employing children in prohibited or hazardous work
laws.fullDescription: Child labor remains a serious problem in Honduras particularly in agriculture, including melon, sugarcane, and coffee production. The law sets the minimum working age at 14 and prohibits hazardous work for those under 18.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years for employers
exceptions: Light supervised family work with school attendance

quiz.q: In which crops is child labor most documented in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Child labor in Honduras is most documented in melon, sugarcane, and coffee production, where children work in physically demanding agricultural conditions.

laws.title: Money Laundering
laws.subtitle: Hiding proceeds of drug trafficking and crime
laws.fullDescription: Given Honduras position as a cocaine transit country and the scale of extortion proceeds, money laundering is a major concern. Drug money is laundered through real estate, businesses, and the financial system. Honduras has strengthened its AML framework under international pressure.
laws.penalty: 15 to 20 years imprisonment; asset confiscation
exceptions: None for knowing participation

quiz.q: What are the primary sources of money laundering in Honduras?
options: Drug trafficking proceeds and extortion income
quiz.explanation: Drug trafficking proceeds and systematic extortion income are the primary sources of funds laundered through the Honduran financial system.

laws.title: Attacks on Journalists and Human Rights Defenders
laws.subtitle: Violence against reporters and activists
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has one of the highest rates of violence against journalists and human rights defenders globally. Reporters covering organized crime and land rights defenders face assassination. The law criminalizes these attacks but impunity is widespread.
laws.penalty: 15 to 30 years imprisonment for killings
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Criminal Code — Attacks on Civil Society

quiz.q: What makes Honduras particularly dangerous for journalists?
options: Covering organized crime makes reporters targets for assassination
quiz.explanation: Journalists who cover organized crime, drug trafficking, and corruption in Honduras face assassination by criminal groups seeking to silence investigative reporting.

laws.title: Coral Reef Destruction
laws.subtitle: Damaging the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef
laws.fullDescription: Honduras Bay Islands sit on the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the world second largest coral reef system. Damaging coral reefs through anchor damage, illegal fishing, chemical pollution, or unauthorized development is prohibited under environmental law.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment; mandatory restoration
exceptions: Scientific research under permits

quiz.q: What is significant about the reef system off Honduras Bay Islands?
options: It is the smallest reef in the world
It is the world second largest coral reef system
quiz.explanation: The Mesoamerican Barrier Reef off Honduras Bay Islands is the world second largest coral reef system, making its protection from damage critically important.

laws.title: Illegal Gambling
laws.subtitle: Operating unlicensed gambling establishments
laws.fullDescription: Honduras requires gambling operations to obtain licenses and comply with regulations. Unlicensed gambling creates opportunities for money laundering and consumer exploitation. Enforcement targets both operators and the criminal networks using gambling fronts.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment for operators
exceptions: State lottery operations

quiz.q: What criminal concern makes unlicensed gambling particularly serious in Honduras?
options: Money laundering through gambling fronts for drug proceeds
quiz.explanation: Unlicensed gambling operations in Honduras frequently serve as fronts for laundering drug trafficking and extortion proceeds.

laws.title: Murder
laws.subtitle: Unlawful intentional killing
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has suffered extremely high murder rates, at times reaching over 90 per 100,000 — among the highest globally. Gang warfare, drug trafficking disputes, and extortion enforcement drive the violence. The criminal code imposes severe penalties.
laws.penalty: 20 to 30 years imprisonment
exceptions: Proportionate self-defense
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Criminal Code — Crimes Against Life

quiz.q: What homicide rate did Honduras reach at its peak?
quiz.explanation: Honduras homicide rate reached over 90 per 100,000 at its peak, making it one of the highest murder rates recorded for any country not at war.

laws.title: Vehicle Theft and Carjacking
laws.subtitle: Stealing vehicles through force or deception
laws.fullDescription: Vehicle theft and armed carjacking are common crimes in Honduras, often connected to criminal networks that strip vehicles or move them across borders. Armed carjacking — stealing vehicles from drivers at gunpoint — carries enhanced penalties.
laws.penalty: 3 to 9 years imprisonment; enhanced for armed carjacking
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What distinguishes carjacking from ordinary vehicle theft?
options: Armed theft from drivers versus unoccupied vehicle theft
quiz.explanation: Carjacking involves armed theft of vehicles from their drivers, while ordinary vehicle theft targets unoccupied vehicles — the presence of violence distinguishes and aggravates the offense.

laws.title: Armed Robbery
laws.subtitle: Theft using weapons or violence
laws.fullDescription: Armed robbery is a major security concern in Honduras, often committed by gang members targeting individuals, businesses, and public transport. The prevalence of firearms makes armed robbery particularly dangerous. Specialized police units respond to armed robbery patterns.
laws.penalty: 9 to 15 years imprisonment; enhanced for injuries or death
exceptions: None

quiz.q: Who most frequently commits armed robbery in Honduras?
options: Gang members targeting businesses and individuals
quiz.explanation: Gang members are the primary perpetrators of armed robbery in Honduras, systematically targeting businesses, transport operators, and individuals.

laws.title: Illegal Fishing
laws.subtitle: Fishing without permits in protected waters
laws.fullDescription: Honduras Caribbean and Pacific coasts have significant marine resources. Illegal fishing — including in marine protected areas, using prohibited methods like dynamite or cyanide fishing, or taking protected species — is a criminal offense enforced by the navy and fisheries authority.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for commercial-scale violations
exceptions: Traditional subsistence fishing by coastal communities within regulations

quiz.q: What prohibited fishing methods are specifically targeted by Honduran enforcement?
quiz.explanation: Dynamite and cyanide fishing are explicitly prohibited destructive methods targeted by Honduran fisheries enforcement due to their devastating impact on reef ecosystems.

laws.title: Cyber Fraud
laws.subtitle: Online scams and digital financial crimes
laws.fullDescription: As internet penetration increases in Honduras, cybercrime has grown. Online fraud targeting bank accounts, wire transfer fraud, and telephone scams are criminalized under Honduras cybercrime framework. The law was updated to address modern digital threats.
laws.penalty: 3 to 6 years imprisonment; restitution of proceeds
exceptions: None

quiz.q: Why has cybercrime grown in Honduras recently?
options: Increasing internet penetration creating more targets
quiz.explanation: As internet access has expanded in Honduras, cybercriminals have found a larger pool of potential victims for online fraud and financial scams.

laws.title: Forced Labor
laws.subtitle: Compelling work through threats or debt bondage
laws.fullDescription: Forced labor including debt bondage has been documented in Honduran agriculture, fishing, and domestic service sectors. Workers — particularly internal migrants and indigenous people — are sometimes trapped through debt manipulation. The law prohibits forced labor in all forms.
laws.penalty: 5 to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — all forced labor is criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Labor Code — Forced Labor Prohibition

quiz.q: In which sectors has forced labor been most documented in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Forced labor and debt bondage have been documented in agricultural, fishing, and domestic service sectors in Honduras, particularly affecting vulnerable migrant workers.

laws.title: Water Source Contamination
laws.subtitle: Polluting rivers or aquifers with toxic waste
laws.fullDescription: Honduras faces serious water quality challenges. Industrial contamination from mining and agriculture threatens drinking water sources. The law prohibits discharge of untreated toxic waste into water bodies and protects watershed areas critical to municipal water supply.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment; mandatory cleanup
exceptions: Permitted discharges within approved environmental impact limits

quiz.q: What industries pose the greatest water contamination risk in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Mining operations and intensive agriculture using chemical inputs pose the greatest water contamination risk in Honduras, threatening drinking water supplies.

laws.title: Cyberstalking and Online Harassment
laws.subtitle: Threatening or harassing people through digital means
laws.fullDescription: Honduras cybercrime legislation addresses online harassment including cyberstalking, distributing intimate images without consent, and systematic digital threats. Women and public figures are frequent victims of coordinated online harassment campaigns.
laws.penalty: 2 to 4 years imprisonment; enhanced for intimate image distribution
exceptions: Legitimate journalism and public interest reporting

quiz.q: Who are the most frequent victims of cyberstalking in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Women and public figures — particularly female politicians and journalists — are the most frequent targets of organized cyberstalking and online harassment in Honduras.

laws.title: Tax Evasion
laws.subtitle: Hiding income to avoid taxes
laws.fullDescription: Honduras government relies on tax revenues to fund social services and infrastructure. Tax evasion — concealing income, submitting false returns, or using offshore accounts — deprives the state of critical resources. The tax authority SAR has increased enforcement.
laws.penalty: Fine of up to 2x taxes owed; up to 5 years imprisonment for large-scale evasion
exceptions: Honest errors and minor discrepancies addressed through amended returns

quiz.q: What is the name of Honduras tax authority?
quiz.explanation: SAR (Servicio de Administracion de Rentas) is Honduras tax administration authority responsible for collecting taxes and enforcing compliance.

laws.title: Terrorism
laws.subtitle: Committing violence for political or ideological goals
laws.fullDescription: Honduras anti-terrorism legislation criminalizes political violence, bombing, and attacks on infrastructure for ideological purposes. Given the Central American context, the law addresses both domestic terrorism risks and the potential for transnational terrorist activity.
laws.penalty: 20 to 30 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — terrorism has no legal justification

quiz.q: What context makes anti-terrorism legislation particularly important in Honduras?
options: Central American regional context and transnational threats
quiz.explanation: Honduras anti-terrorism laws address both domestic risks and Central America regional context, including potential transnational terrorism activity in a region with significant organized crime.

laws.title: Illegal Mining
laws.subtitle: Extracting minerals without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has significant mineral resources and mining is economically important. However, illegal artisanal mining and unauthorized industrial extraction cause environmental damage, particularly contaminating rivers with mercury and cyanide. Protests against mining projects have been violently suppressed.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment; equipment confiscation
exceptions: Licensed mining operations with approved environmental impact assessments

quiz.q: What environmental hazard is associated with illegal mining in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Illegal mining operations in Honduras contaminate rivers with mercury and cyanide, posing serious risks to drinking water and aquatic ecosystems.

laws.title: Blackmail
laws.subtitle: Threatening exposure to extort money or favors
laws.fullDescription: Blackmail — threatening to expose embarrassing or damaging information unless payment or favors are received — is criminalized in Honduras. Digital blackmail using intimate photos or videos (sextortion) has grown as a major concern with increased smartphone use.
laws.penalty: 3 to 6 years imprisonment
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Criminal Code — Extortion and Blackmail

quiz.q: What type of blackmail has grown with increased smartphone use in Honduras?
options: Sextortion using intimate photos or videos
quiz.explanation: Sextortion — blackmail using intimate photos or videos — has grown significantly in Honduras alongside increased smartphone use and social media access.

laws.title: Maritime Drug Smuggling
laws.subtitle: Transporting drugs by sea
laws.fullDescription: Honduras coastlines — both Caribbean and Pacific — are used for cocaine shipments. Go-fast boats, semi-submersibles, and fishing vessels are used to move drugs. The Honduran navy intercepts shipments with US DEA cooperation. Maritime trafficking carries severe penalties.
laws.penalty: 15 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What types of vessels are used for maritime drug smuggling in Honduras?
options: Go-fast boats, semi-submersibles, and fishing vessels
quiz.explanation: Drug smugglers use go-fast boats, semi-submersible vessels, and disguised fishing boats to move cocaine through Honduran coastal waters.

laws.title: Illegal Waste Dumping
laws.subtitle: Dumping industrial or hazardous waste illegally
laws.fullDescription: Illegal dumping of industrial waste, medical waste, and solid waste outside approved facilities is a significant environmental problem in Honduras. Waste pollutes rivers, contaminates soil, and creates public health risks. Municipal and industrial violations are both prosecuted.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for hazardous waste violations
exceptions: Emergency spill response procedures

quiz.q: What waste types carry the most serious legal penalties when illegally dumped?
quiz.explanation: Illegal dumping of hazardous waste — including industrial chemicals and medical waste — carries the most serious penalties under Honduras environmental law.

laws.title: Illegal Squatting on Private Land
laws.subtitle: Occupying land without the owner consent
laws.fullDescription: Land invasions and illegal squatting on private land are recurring conflicts in Honduras, driven by extreme inequality and landlessness. While poverty drives many such actions, the law protects property rights and landowners may seek court eviction orders.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment; eviction order
exceptions: Adverse possession claims meeting statutory requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Civil and Criminal Code — Property

quiz.q: What underlying social condition drives illegal squatting in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Extreme land inequality and widespread landlessness drive illegal land occupation in Honduras, creating recurring conflicts between landless farmers and large landowners.

laws.title: Prescription Drug Abuse and Illegal Sale
laws.subtitle: Selling prescription medications without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Honduras regulates pharmaceutical sales and prohibits the dispensing of prescription medications without a valid prescription. The black market sale of controlled medications — including opioids and benzodiazepines — is criminalized to protect public health.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for commercial violations
exceptions: Licensed pharmacists acting within regulations

quiz.q: What regulatory requirement protects consumers when buying medications in Honduras?
options: Valid prescription requirement for controlled medications
quiz.explanation: Honduras requires valid prescriptions for controlled medications as a consumer protection measure and to prevent abuse of opioids, benzodiazepines, and other controlled substances.

laws.title: Sabotage of Critical Infrastructure
laws.subtitle: Damaging power, water, or communications systems
laws.fullDescription: Honduras criminal law imposes severe penalties for deliberate attacks on critical infrastructure including power systems, water treatment plants, communications networks, and fuel distribution. Such attacks can paralyze essential services for millions of people.
laws.penalty: 10 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Accidental damage — only deliberate sabotage is criminalized

quiz.q: Why are infrastructure attacks particularly serious in Honduras?
options: They can paralyze essential services for millions of people
quiz.explanation: Attacks on Honduras infrastructure — power, water, and communications — can rapidly paralyze essential services for large populations in a country with limited redundancy.

laws.title: Identity Theft
laws.subtitle: Stealing personal information to commit fraud
laws.fullDescription: Identity theft — using stolen personal information to fraudulently obtain credit, benefits, or access — is criminalized under Honduras computer crimes law. Digital databases and healthcare records are particular targets for identity thieves operating in financial fraud networks.
laws.penalty: 3 to 6 years imprisonment; restitution
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Computer Crimes Act — Identity Theft

quiz.q: What types of records are particularly targeted by identity thieves in Honduras?
options: Digital databases and healthcare records for financial fraud
quiz.explanation: Digital databases and healthcare records are particularly targeted by identity thieves in Honduras to create fraudulent financial accounts or medical billing fraud.

laws.title: Workplace Safety Violations
laws.subtitle: Ignoring required safety standards for workers
laws.fullDescription: Honduras labor code requires employers to provide safe working conditions and protective equipment. Violations are common particularly in agriculture, construction, and manufacturing. The Labor Inspectorate enforces standards and can impose fines and close unsafe operations.
laws.penalty: Fine; closure of facility for egregious violations
exceptions: Small-scale family enterprises with limited regulatory scope

quiz.q: Which industries have the most workplace safety violations in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Agriculture, construction, and manufacturing have the highest rates of workplace safety violations in Honduras, with workers exposed to unguarded machinery, toxic chemicals, and structural hazards.

laws.title: Possession of Illegal Ammunition
laws.subtitle: Having prohibited caliber bullets without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Honduras firearms law restricts not only weapons but also ammunition. Civilian possession of military-grade ammunition — such as armor-piercing rounds and high-caliber rifle cartridges — is prohibited. This complements the firearms law in restricting gang armaments.
laws.penalty: 2 to 6 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed security and military personnel within regulations
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Firearms and Ammunition Control Act

quiz.q: What types of ammunition are specifically prohibited for civilian possession in Honduras?
options: Military-grade ammunition such as armor-piercing rounds
quiz.explanation: Military-grade ammunition — including armor-piercing rounds and high-caliber rifle cartridges — is prohibited for civilian possession in Honduras to restrict gang armaments.

laws.title: Forced Displacement
laws.subtitle: Driving families from their homes through threats
laws.fullDescription: Forced displacement — compelling families to abandon their homes and communities through gang threats, extortion demands, or violence — affects hundreds of thousands of Hondurans. The criminal code addresses this as both a criminal act and a human rights violation.
laws.penalty: 10 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — forced displacement is always criminal

quiz.q: How many Hondurans have been affected by gang-related forced displacement?
quiz.explanation: Hundreds of thousands of Hondurans have been forcibly displaced from their homes and communities by gang threats, extortion demands, and violence.

laws.title: Fraudulent Business Registration
laws.subtitle: Registering companies with false information
laws.fullDescription: Honduras business registration law requires accurate disclosure of ownership and activities. Registering shell companies with false ownership information is used to hide criminal proceeds, evade taxes, and facilitate fraud. The mercantile registry and SAR both monitor for fraudulent registrations.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment; business dissolution
exceptions: Corrections made voluntarily before enforcement action

quiz.q: What criminal purpose most commonly drives fraudulent business registration in Honduras?
options: Hiding criminal proceeds and evading taxes
quiz.explanation: Fraudulent business registrations in Honduras are most commonly used to create shell companies that hide criminal proceeds and facilitate tax evasion.

laws.title: Child Recruitment by Gangs
laws.subtitle: Recruiting minors into criminal organizations
laws.fullDescription: MS-13 and Barrio 18 actively recruit children and adolescents in Honduras, offering money and protection while exposing them to violence and criminality. The law specifically criminalizes the recruitment of minors into criminal gangs with enhanced penalties.
laws.penalty: 12 to 18 years imprisonment for recruiters
exceptions: None

quiz.q: Why do gangs specifically target children and adolescents for recruitment in Honduras?
options: Minors are legally exempt from prosecution
They are vulnerable, controllable, and face lighter penalties if caught
quiz.explanation: Gangs target minors because they are psychologically vulnerable, easier to control, and in Honduras historically faced lighter legal consequences — making them useful to criminal organizations.

laws.title: Agricultural Land Burning
laws.subtitle: Setting fire to fields without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Uncontrolled burning of agricultural land is a major environmental problem in Honduras causing air pollution, soil degradation, and risk of wildfire spread. The environmental authority SERNA prohibits field burning outside designated periods and without permits.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years for fires causing serious damage
exceptions: Controlled burning with prior permits during approved periods

quiz.q: Which government body regulates agricultural burning permits in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: SERNA (Secretaria de Recursos Naturales y Ambiente) is Honduras environmental authority responsible for issuing and enforcing agricultural burning permits.

laws.title: Human Trafficking for Entertainment
laws.subtitle: Exploiting people in performance or sex tourism
laws.fullDescription: Beyond labor trafficking, Honduras law specifically addresses trafficking for entertainment including sexual exploitation in tourism contexts. The Bay Islands and urban centers have been identified as locations where sex tourism targeting trafficked individuals occurs.
laws.penalty: 12 to 18 years imprisonment; enhanced for minors
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Law Against Human Trafficking — Tourism

quiz.q: Where have sex tourism operations been identified in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Honduras Bay Islands tourist areas and major urban centers have been identified by authorities as locations where sex tourism involving trafficked individuals takes place.

laws.title: Credit Card Fraud
laws.subtitle: Using stolen card data for unauthorized purchases
laws.fullDescription: Credit card cloning, skimming device installations, and stolen card data use are criminalized under Honduras financial crime laws. As electronic payments have spread, financial fraud targeting card users has grown, affecting banks and consumers.
laws.penalty: 3 to 6 years imprisonment; restitution
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What technical method is used to steal card information at point-of-sale in Honduras?
options: Skimming devices installed on card readers
quiz.explanation: Skimming devices secretly installed on ATMs and point-of-sale terminals are commonly used to steal credit and debit card data in Honduras for fraudulent transactions.

laws.title: Arson
laws.subtitle: Deliberately setting fire to property
laws.fullDescription: Arson — intentionally setting fire to property — is a serious crime in Honduras. Fires are sometimes set as gang enforcement tools, to destroy evidence, or in business disputes. The law imposes severe penalties, enhanced when arson endangers human life.
laws.penalty: 5 to 12 years imprisonment; enhanced to 20 years if lives endangered
exceptions: None — deliberate fire-setting is always criminal

quiz.q: How is arson sometimes used as a criminal tool in Honduras?
options: Gang enforcement, evidence destruction, or business disputes
quiz.explanation: Arson in Honduras is often used as a gang enforcement tool — burning the property of those who refuse to pay extortion — or to destroy evidence of criminal activity.

laws.title: Road Blockades Without Authorization
laws.subtitle: Obstructing public roads illegally
laws.fullDescription: Blocking public roads as a form of protest or extortion is illegal in Honduras without authorization. While legitimate protest includes the right to demonstrate, permanently blocking roads disrupts commerce and emergency services. Criminal gangs sometimes establish unauthorized checkpoints.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment; enhanced for extortion at checkpoints
exceptions: Authorized demonstrations with prior notification and police coordination

quiz.q: What criminal purpose do illegal roadblocks sometimes serve in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Criminal gangs in Honduras sometimes establish unauthorized road checkpoints as a form of extortion, demanding payment from drivers — a criminal abuse of road control.

laws.title: Illegal Adoption Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Selling children through false adoption processes
laws.fullDescription: Honduras was forced to suspend international adoptions due to widespread fraud and child trafficking through the adoption system. Children were illegally obtained from families through deception, coercion, and forgery to feed demand from foreign adopters. The law now strictly criminalizes these practices.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment for organizers
exceptions: Legitimate intercountry adoption under reformed legal framework

quiz.q: Why did Honduras suspend international adoptions?
options: Widespread fraud and child trafficking through the adoption system
quiz.explanation: Honduras suspended international adoptions because widespread fraud and child trafficking — children taken from families through deception and sold to foreign adopters — had corrupted the adoption system.

laws.title: Illegal Plant Collection from Protected Areas
laws.subtitle: Removing plants or orchids from national parks
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has exceptional plant biodiversity including rare orchids in cloud forests and medicinal plants in indigenous territories. Removing plants — particularly commercially valuable orchids — from protected areas violates environmental law and can damage ecosystems.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment for commercial scale
exceptions: Scientific research under permits; indigenous traditional use within regulations

quiz.q: What plant type is most commercially targeted for illegal collection in Honduras protected areas?
quiz.explanation: Rare orchids in Honduran cloud forests are highly valuable commercially and are targeted by illegal collectors for the international ornamental plant trade.

laws.title: Contempt of Court
laws.subtitle: Defying or disrupting court proceedings
laws.fullDescription: Honduras judicial system criminalizes contempt of court — willful refusal to comply with court orders, disrupting proceedings, or threatening judges and court officials. Given the pervasive influence of criminal networks on the justice system, contempt protection supports judicial independence.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 18 months imprisonment
exceptions: Good faith legal challenges to court orders through proper channels
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Organic Law of the Judiciary

quiz.q: Why is contempt of court protection particularly important in Honduras?
options: Supporting judicial independence against criminal network pressure
quiz.explanation: Contempt of court protections are especially important in Honduras because criminal networks and corrupt interests have historically tried to intimidate and pressure the judiciary.

laws.title: Counterfeiting Currency
laws.subtitle: Manufacturing or distributing fake money
laws.fullDescription: Counterfeiting Honduras lempira or foreign currencies is a serious financial crime. Counterfeit currency destabilizes commerce and harms those who unwittingly accept fake notes. Honduras Central Bank and police cooperate to detect and prosecute counterfeiting operations.
laws.penalty: 5 to 12 years imprisonment
exceptions: Clearly marked replicas for educational or theatrical purposes

quiz.q: Which institution cooperates with police to detect currency counterfeiting in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Honduras Central Bank (Banco Central de Honduras) works with law enforcement to detect counterfeit currency and prosecute counterfeiting operations.

laws.title: Sea Turtle Poaching
laws.subtitle: Killing or stealing eggs from sea turtles
laws.fullDescription: Honduras Caribbean and Pacific coasts are nesting grounds for several sea turtle species including leatherback, hawksbill, and loggerhead turtles. Poaching turtle eggs — a traditional but now illegal practice — and killing turtles for meat or shell are criminal offenses.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — all sea turtle poaching is prohibited

quiz.q: What makes Honduras coastlines significant for sea turtle conservation?
options: They are nesting grounds for multiple sea turtle species
Only one species uses Honduran beaches
Turtle farming is the primary activity
quiz.explanation: Honduras Caribbean and Pacific coasts serve as nesting grounds for multiple sea turtle species — leatherback, hawksbill, and loggerhead — making protection of nesting beaches critical to species survival.

laws.title: Theft of Public Utilities
laws.subtitle: Illegal electricity or water connections
laws.fullDescription: Unauthorized tapping of electricity, water, or telecommunications infrastructure is widespread in Honduras, particularly in informal urban settlements. These illegal connections deprive public utilities of revenue needed for maintenance and expansion, while creating safety hazards.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment for repeated violations
exceptions: Emergency humanitarian connections authorized by courts

quiz.q: Where is unauthorized utility connection most prevalent in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Unauthorized electricity and water connections are most common in informal urban settlements in Honduras, where residents lacking formal connections tap into existing infrastructure.

laws.title: Weapons Manufacturing Without License
laws.subtitle: Producing firearms without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Manufacturing firearms without a government license is a serious crime in Honduras. Clandestine weapons workshops supply criminals with illegal arms. Homemade and converted weapons — particularly machine pistols — are used in gang violence.
laws.penalty: 10 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed gunmakers within legal framework

quiz.q: What type of illegal weapon has been associated with clandestine manufacturing in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Clandestine workshops in Honduras have been found converting semi-automatic pistols to fire automatically — creating illegal machine pistols used in gang violence.

laws.title: Illegal Land Speculation
laws.subtitle: Manipulating land registries for profit
laws.fullDescription: Land fraud — including forging title deeds, manipulating the property registry, and using corrupt officials to fraudulently transfer land — is a significant problem in Honduras. Indigenous communities and rural farmers are frequently victims of land fraud by powerful interests.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 8 years imprisonment; restoration of land rights
exceptions: Legitimate property transactions with proper documentation

quiz.q: Who are the most common victims of land fraud in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Indigenous communities and rural farmers are the most frequent victims of land fraud in Honduras, losing ancestral and agricultural lands to forged titles and corrupt registry manipulation.

laws.title: Contaminated Food Production
laws.subtitle: Knowingly selling unsafe or adulterated food
laws.fullDescription: Honduras food safety laws require food producers and distributors to meet hygiene standards. Knowingly producing or selling contaminated, adulterated, or mislabeled food that poses health risks is criminalized. Enforcement is conducted by the health regulatory authority ARSA.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment for knowing violations causing illness
exceptions: Honest errors promptly corrected upon discovery

quiz.q: What is the name of Honduras food safety regulatory authority?
quiz.explanation: ARSA (Agencia de Regulacion Sanitaria) is Honduras regulatory authority responsible for food safety, pharmaceutical oversight, and health product standards.

laws.title: Computer System Hacking
laws.subtitle: Unauthorized access to digital systems
laws.fullDescription: Unauthorized access to computer systems — hacking — is criminalized under Honduras computer crimes legislation. This includes accessing banking systems, government databases, and private corporate networks without authorization. Given growing digital infrastructure, cybersecurity enforcement has increased.
laws.penalty: 3 to 6 years imprisonment; enhanced for critical infrastructure
exceptions: Authorized penetration testing under written agreements
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Computer Crimes Act — Unauthorized Access

quiz.q: What circumstance can legally justify accessing a computer system that would otherwise be hacking?
options: Authorized penetration testing with written agreements
quiz.explanation: Authorized penetration testing — security testing conducted under written agreement with the system owner — is the legitimate exception to computer access crime laws.

laws.title: Industrial Air Pollution
laws.subtitle: Emitting toxic gases beyond permitted levels
laws.fullDescription: Honduras environmental law sets limits on industrial air emissions. Factories, power plants, and processing facilities that exceed permitted emission levels for toxic gases damage public health and violate environmental standards enforced by SERNA.
laws.penalty: Fine; mandatory emission controls installation; facility closure for persistent violations
exceptions: Permitted emissions within environmental impact assessment limits

quiz.q: What type of facility most commonly violates air emission standards in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Industrial factories and processing plants are the most common violators of air emission standards in Honduras, emitting dust, fumes, and chemical gases beyond permitted levels.

laws.title: Impersonating Law Enforcement
laws.subtitle: Posing as police or military to commit crimes
laws.fullDescription: Criminal gangs in Honduras sometimes impersonate police officers or military personnel to set up false checkpoints, conduct fake raids, and rob victims who comply with their false authority. The criminal code imposes severe penalties for impersonating law enforcement.
laws.penalty: 5 to 10 years imprisonment; enhanced for crimes committed during impersonation
exceptions: None — law enforcement impersonation is always criminal

quiz.q: How do criminal groups exploit law enforcement impersonation in Honduras?
options: False checkpoints and fake raids to rob victims
quiz.explanation: Criminal gangs in Honduras impersonate police and military to set up fake checkpoints and conduct false raids — exploiting citizen compliance with apparent authority to rob victims.

laws.title: Academic Credential Fraud
laws.subtitle: Falsely claiming degrees or professional licenses
laws.fullDescription: Falsely claiming professional credentials — especially medical, legal, or engineering licenses — is a criminal offense in Honduras. The practice poses serious risks when unqualified practitioners provide medical care or legal advice based on fraudulent credentials.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment; license revocation
exceptions: None for practicing regulated professions without genuine credentials

quiz.q: Why is credential fraud particularly dangerous in Honduras?
options: Unqualified practitioners in medicine and law risk serious harm to clients
quiz.explanation: Credential fraud in Honduras poses serious public safety risks when unqualified people practice medicine, law, or engineering based on fraudulent credentials, potentially harming clients.

laws.title: Contract Killing
laws.subtitle: Hiring someone to commit murder for payment
laws.fullDescription: Honduras criminal code imposes maximum penalties for contract killing — hiring or being hired to commit murder for payment. The country struggles with high rates of contract killings connected to organized crime, gang disputes, and business conflicts.
laws.penalty: 30 years imprisonment
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What contexts generate most contract killings in Honduras?
options: Organized crime, gang disputes, and business conflicts
quiz.explanation: Contract killings in Honduras are primarily connected to organized crime enforcement, gang territorial disputes, and business conflicts where murder is used to resolve commercial disagreements.

laws.title: Illegal Crocodile Hunting
laws.subtitle: Hunting or capturing protected reptiles
laws.fullDescription: American crocodiles inhabit Honduras rivers and coastal areas. Hunting crocodiles for their skin, meat, or capturing them for the pet trade is prohibited under wildlife protection law. The species is protected as part of Honduras biodiversity heritage.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorized research and conservation programs

quiz.q: Why are crocodiles protected in Honduras?
options: They are part of Honduras biodiversity heritage and face hunting pressure
quiz.explanation: American crocodiles are protected in Honduras as part of the country biodiversity heritage, facing threats from hunting for their valuable skin and capture for the pet trade.

laws.title: School Bus Extortion
laws.subtitle: Extorting drivers and operators of school transport
laws.fullDescription: Criminal gangs systematically extort school bus operators across Honduras, charging war tax on routes serving students. This extortion has led to school service disruptions when operators cannot pay or refuse. The criminalization of this practice carries enhanced penalties for targeting children services.
laws.penalty: 13 to 18 years imprisonment — enhanced for targeting school services
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Criminal Code — Extortion Enhanced Penalties

quiz.q: What consequence has gang extortion of school buses caused in Honduras?
options: Service disruptions when operators cannot pay
quiz.explanation: Gang extortion of school bus operators has caused service disruptions across Honduras when operators unable or unwilling to pay the war tax suspended services.

laws.title: Pyramid Schemes
laws.subtitle: Operating investment frauds promising false returns
laws.fullDescription: Pyramid and Ponzi schemes have defrauded Honduran investors repeatedly. These fraud operations promise unsustainable returns and collapse inevitably, leaving investors with losses. Honduras financial regulatory commission CNBS prohibits and prosecutes pyramid scheme operators.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 8 years imprisonment for organizers
exceptions: Legitimate multi-level marketing with genuine product sales
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Financial Crimes Act — Investment Fraud

quiz.q: Which body regulates financial products and prosecutes pyramid schemes in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: CNBS (Comision Nacional de Bancos y Seguros) is Honduras financial regulatory body responsible for overseeing financial products and prosecuting pyramid scheme operators.

laws.title: Unauthorized Recording and Privacy Violations
laws.subtitle: Secretly recording people in private situations
laws.fullDescription: Honduras criminal law protects personal privacy, prohibiting secret recording of individuals in private settings without consent and distribution of such recordings. The law aims to balance freedom of information with protection of personal dignity and privacy.
laws.penalty: 2 to 4 years imprisonment; enhanced for distribution
exceptions: Journalism and law enforcement recording within legal framework

quiz.q: What legitimate purpose can justify recording individuals in Honduras?
options: Journalism and authorized law enforcement within legal framework
quiz.explanation: Legitimate journalism and authorized law enforcement operations can legally record individuals within the framework established by Honduran law.

laws.title: Pregnancy Discrimination
laws.subtitle: Firing or refusing to hire pregnant workers
laws.fullDescription: Honduras labor law prohibits dismissal of pregnant employees and discrimination in hiring based on pregnancy. Women must be permitted to take maternity leave and return to equivalent positions. Enforcement is handled by the Labor Inspectorate, though many violations go unreported.
laws.penalty: Fine; reinstatement order; compensation for lost wages
exceptions: None — pregnancy discrimination is always prohibited

quiz.q: What remedy can a dismissed pregnant worker seek in Honduras?
options: Fine against employer; reinstatement; compensation for lost wages
quiz.explanation: A pregnant worker illegally dismissed in Honduras can seek a fine against the employer, reinstatement to her position, and compensation for wages lost during unlawful dismissal.

laws.title: Surveillance for Criminal Purposes
laws.subtitle: Spying on targets for gangs or criminal organizations
laws.fullDescription: Criminal organizations in Honduras use surveillance operatives — called halcones (hawks) — to monitor police, track rivals, and identify extortion targets. Conducting surveillance for criminal purposes is criminalized as participation in organized crime activity.
laws.penalty: 6 to 12 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorized law enforcement surveillance with judicial orders

quiz.q: What term is used in Honduras for gang surveillance operatives?
quiz.explanation: Gang surveillance operatives in Honduras are known as halcones (hawks) — individuals paid to monitor police movements, track rivals, and identify targets for extortion or violence.

laws.title: Neglect of Epidemic Disease Reporting
laws.subtitle: Failing to report notifiable disease outbreaks
laws.fullDescription: Honduras public health law requires healthcare providers to report cases of notifiable diseases to health authorities. Failure to report dengue, cholera, and other epidemic diseases delays outbreak response and endangers communities. Honduras has experienced major dengue and cholera outbreaks.
laws.penalty: Fine for healthcare providers; administrative sanctions
exceptions: Good faith errors in uncertain diagnoses
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Public Health Act — Disease Reporting

quiz.q: Which diseases have caused major outbreaks in Honduras requiring mandatory reporting?
quiz.explanation: Dengue fever and cholera have caused major outbreaks in Honduras, making timely mandatory reporting by healthcare providers critical to outbreak containment.

laws.title: Illegal Migration by Sea
laws.subtitle: Unauthorized border crossing through coastal waters
laws.fullDescription: Honduras coastline is used for unauthorized migration as well as drug smuggling. People attempting to enter other countries by sea without authorization — particularly to reach the United States through the Gulf — face prosecution. The law distinguishes personal migration from profiting from smuggling others.
laws.penalty: Fine; deportation for personal illegal entry; 6 to 12 years for smuggling
exceptions: Recognized refugees and asylum seekers under international law

quiz.q: How does Honduras law distinguish between personal illegal migration and smuggling?
options: Personal entry faces fines and deportation; profiting from smuggling others faces imprisonment
quiz.explanation: Honduras law distinguishes between a person illegally entering another country (fine and deportation) and those who profit from smuggling others — a much more serious crime carrying imprisonment.

laws.title: Illegal Sand and Gravel Extraction
laws.subtitle: Mining riverbeds and beaches without permits
laws.fullDescription: Illegal extraction of sand and gravel from rivers and beaches is widespread in Honduras and causes serious environmental damage including river bank erosion, flooding risk, and loss of aquatic habitat. Construction demand drives illegal extraction operations.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for commercial-scale operations
exceptions: Licensed extraction operations within approved volumes

quiz.q: What environmental harm results from illegal sand and gravel extraction in Honduras?
options: River bank erosion, flooding risk, and aquatic habitat loss
quiz.explanation: Illegal riverbed sand extraction in Honduras causes bank erosion, increases flooding risk by altering river channels, and destroys the aquatic habitat of fish and other species.

laws.title: Obstruction of Justice
laws.subtitle: Interfering with investigations or witnesses
laws.fullDescription: Obstructing justice — bribing or threatening witnesses, destroying evidence, or interfering with judicial proceedings — is criminalized in Honduras. Given widespread criminal influence over courts and witnesses, obstruction of justice undermines accountability for serious crimes.
laws.penalty: 5 to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Legitimate legal advice to clients within professional ethics

quiz.q: How does criminal network influence manifest as obstruction in Honduras?
options: Bribing and threatening witnesses and judicial officials
quiz.explanation: Criminal networks in Honduras obstruct justice by bribing or threatening witnesses, intimidating judicial officials, and destroying evidence to prevent accountability for serious crimes.

laws.title: Illegal Online Gaming and Betting
laws.subtitle: Operating unlicensed online gambling platforms
laws.fullDescription: The rapid growth of online gambling platforms has created regulatory challenges in Honduras. Operating online gambling without a license from the regulatory authority is prohibited. Unlicensed platforms avoid consumer protections and anti-money laundering requirements.
laws.penalty: Fine; platform shutdown; up to 2 years for operators
exceptions: Licensed online platforms under regulatory framework
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Gambling Regulation Act — Online Platforms

quiz.q: What consumer protection concern drives online gambling regulation in Honduras?
options: Unlicensed platforms avoid consumer protections and AML requirements
quiz.explanation: Regulating online gambling in Honduras protects consumers from unscrupulous operators and ensures platforms comply with anti-money laundering requirements that licensed operators must follow.

laws.title: Police Corruption and Extortion
laws.subtitle: Officers demanding bribes or committing crimes
laws.fullDescription: Corruption within the Honduran National Police has been a major institutional problem. Officers extorting drivers, taking bribes from criminals, or protecting drug shipments face prosecution. Honduras has conducted major police purges removing thousands of corrupt officers.
laws.penalty: Dismissal; 6 to 12 years imprisonment depending on violation
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Criminal Code — Corruption; Police Reform Act

quiz.q: What major institutional action has Honduras taken against police corruption?
options: Mass police purges removing thousands of corrupt officers
quiz.explanation: Honduras conducted major police purges that removed thousands of officers who failed integrity tests or were implicated in corruption — one of the largest institutional anti-corruption efforts in Central America.

laws.title: Mangrove Destruction
laws.subtitle: Clearing coastal mangrove forests
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has significant mangrove ecosystems along both coasts that protect against storms, support fisheries, and sequester carbon. Destruction of mangroves for aquaculture, tourism development, or urban expansion is prohibited. Honduras Caribbean coast has some of the most significant mangrove forests in the region.
laws.penalty: Fine; mandatory restoration; up to 5 years for large-scale destruction
exceptions: Permitted projects with environmental impact assessments and mitigation plans

quiz.q: What environmental functions do mangroves provide on the Honduras coast?
options: Storm protection, fishery support, and carbon sequestration
quiz.explanation: Honduras mangroves provide storm surge protection, serve as nurseries for fisheries, and sequester significant amounts of carbon — making their preservation critical for both ecology and climate.

laws.title: Theft from Public Transport
laws.subtitle: Robbery on buses and taxis
laws.fullDescription: Robbery on public buses and taxis is a chronic security problem in Honduras. Armed robberies targeting passengers on urban and intercity bus routes are common. The Honduran National Police has anti-extortion units that also address public transport crime.
laws.penalty: 5 to 9 years imprisonment; enhanced for armed robbery
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Criminal Code — Armed Robbery in Transport

quiz.q: What police unit addresses both extortion and public transport robbery in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Honduras National Police anti-extortion units (ATIC) handle both the systematic extortion of transport operators and armed robbery on public buses and taxis.

laws.title: Alcohol Sales to Minors
laws.subtitle: Selling alcohol to persons under 18
laws.fullDescription: Honduras prohibits the sale of alcoholic beverages to minors under 18 years of age. Despite the prohibition, enforcement is inconsistent particularly in informal settings. Underage drinking is linked to traffic accidents, violence, and school dropout rates.
laws.penalty: Fine for retailers; license suspension for repeat violations
exceptions: None — sales to minors are always prohibited

quiz.q: What social problems are linked to underage alcohol consumption in Honduras?
options: Traffic accidents, violence, and school dropout rates
quiz.explanation: Underage alcohol consumption in Honduras is linked to increased traffic accidents, youth violence, and school dropout rates — driving the prohibition on sales to those under 18.

laws.title: Fuel Theft and Smuggling
laws.subtitle: Stealing petroleum products or smuggling fuel across borders
laws.fullDescription: Fuel theft — including tapping pipelines and stealing from storage facilities — costs Honduras millions annually. Fuel smuggling from subsidized neighboring countries exploits price differences. Both activities are criminalized as theft and contraband.
laws.penalty: 5 to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: None
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Criminal Code — Energy Theft and Contraband

quiz.q: How does fuel smuggling exploit regional price differences in Honduras?
options: Smugglers import subsidized fuel from neighboring countries to sell at profit
Only domestic theft is an issue
Fuel smuggling goes through official channels
quiz.explanation: Fuel smugglers import petroleum products from countries with government subsidies at lower prices and sell them at profit in Honduras — undermining legal fuel markets and tax revenues.

laws.title: Domestic Violence
laws.subtitle: Physical or psychological violence within the family
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has criminalized domestic violence as a standalone offense with specific protections including restraining orders and emergency shelter access. Domestic violence is linked to broader patterns of gender violence and gang culture. Specialized domestic violence courts handle cases.
laws.penalty: 1 to 3 years imprisonment; restraining orders; victim protection measures
exceptions: None — domestic violence is always criminal

quiz.q: What specialized legal mechanism does Honduras use for domestic violence cases?
quiz.explanation: Honduras established specialized domestic violence courts to handle cases with appropriate expertise and victim-centered procedures, including emergency protection measures.

laws.title: Intellectual Property Piracy
laws.subtitle: Selling counterfeit goods or pirated media
laws.fullDescription: Pirated software, counterfeit clothing brands, and illegal music and film copies are sold openly in Honduran markets. Honduras intellectual property law prohibits commercial-scale piracy and counterfeiting. Enforcement is conducted by prosecutors and customs officials.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment for commercial-scale operations
exceptions: Personal use of limited quantities within fair use doctrine

quiz.q: In what settings is intellectual property piracy most openly visible in Honduras?
options: Open-air markets selling counterfeit goods and pirated media
quiz.explanation: Intellectual property piracy in Honduras is most visible in open-air markets where counterfeit branded goods, pirated software, and copied music and films are sold openly.

laws.title: Illegal Herbicide Use near Water Sources
laws.subtitle: Applying chemicals in protected watershed areas
laws.fullDescription: Honduras law prohibits the application of herbicides and pesticides within protected buffer zones around rivers, lakes, and reservoirs. Chemical contamination of water sources from agricultural runoff is a major threat to drinking water quality in rural areas.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years for violations causing water contamination
exceptions: Approved products used within regulatory buffer requirements

quiz.q: What area type has the strictest restrictions on herbicide use in Honduras?
options: Buffer zones around rivers, lakes, and reservoirs
quiz.explanation: Protected buffer zones around Honduran rivers, lakes, and reservoirs have the strictest herbicide application restrictions to prevent chemical contamination of drinking water sources.

laws.title: Crimes Against Humanity
laws.subtitle: Systematic atrocities against civilian populations
laws.fullDescription: Honduras criminal code incorporates international standards on crimes against humanity following the civil war era abuses committed by Battalion 3-16 and other security forces. Systematic persecution, forced disappearance, and extrajudicial killings are criminalized with no statute of limitations.
laws.penalty: 30 years imprisonment; no statute of limitations
exceptions: None — crimes against humanity cannot be amnestied or pardoned

quiz.q: What historical unit committed crimes against humanity in Honduras during the 1980s?
quiz.explanation: Battalion 3-16 was a secret Honduran military intelligence unit that committed systematic forced disappearances, torture, and extrajudicial killings during the 1980s — crimes now prosecutable under international law.

laws.title: Illegal Street Vending Extortion
laws.subtitle: Gangs taxing informal market vendors
laws.fullDescription: Gang extortion extends throughout Honduras informal economy, with market vendors, street sellers, and small businesses all subject to war tax demands. Failure to pay results in violence or property destruction. Anti-extortion units target organized extortion of market communities.
laws.penalty: 9 to 13 years imprisonment for extortionists
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What term describes the gang tax imposed on street vendors in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: Street vendors in Honduras are subject to impuesto de guerra (war tax) demands from the gang controlling their area — an extortion system that pervades the informal economy.

laws.title: Witness Intimidation
laws.subtitle: Threatening or harming witnesses to crimes
laws.fullDescription: Witness intimidation is endemic in Honduras, where criminal organizations systematically threaten, assault, or kill witnesses in criminal proceedings. The result is widespread witness silence and impunity for serious crimes. Honduras has witness protection programs but resources are limited.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment for witness intimidation; enhanced if witness is killed
exceptions: None

quiz.q: What is the consequence of widespread witness intimidation for Honduras justice system?
options: Witness silence leading to widespread impunity for crimes
quiz.explanation: Systematic witness intimidation in Honduras leads to witness silence — unwillingness to testify — which produces widespread impunity as criminal cases collapse without testimony.

laws.title: Arson in Protected Forests
laws.subtitle: Deliberately burning national parks or forest reserves
laws.fullDescription: Deliberate forest fires in protected areas — whether for land clearing, retaliation, or criminal concealment — are among the most serious environmental crimes in Honduras. The country loses thousands of hectares of forest annually to arson and uncontrolled burns.
laws.penalty: Up to 10 years imprisonment; mandatory reforestation costs
exceptions: Prescribed burns under permit in non-protected areas
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Forest Protection Act — Fire Crimes

quiz.q: How many hectares does Honduras lose to fires annually?
quiz.explanation: Honduras loses thousands of hectares of forest annually to fires — a combination of deliberate arson for land clearing and uncontrolled burns spreading from agricultural areas into protected forests.

laws.title: Contraband Goods Smuggling
laws.subtitle: Importing goods to evade customs duties
laws.fullDescription: Contraband smuggling — importing goods without paying customs duties — deprives Honduras of revenue and undermines legitimate business. Common contraband includes electronics, clothing, cigarettes, and alcohol. Customs officers and organized networks are involved in commercial-scale smuggling.
laws.penalty: Fine of up to 3x duties owed; up to 6 years for commercial-scale smuggling
exceptions: Personal duty-free allowances within permitted limits

quiz.q: What goods are most commonly smuggled into Honduras to evade customs duties?
quiz.explanation: Electronics, clothing, cigarettes, and alcohol are the most commonly smuggled goods in Honduras — high-demand consumer products where the duty savings make smuggling profitable.

laws.title: Attacks on Healthcare Workers
laws.subtitle: Violence against doctors, nurses, and ambulances
laws.fullDescription: Attacks on healthcare workers and medical facilities — including shooting at ambulances in gang-controlled territories — are criminalized in Honduras with enhanced penalties. Healthcare workers trying to treat gang members or crime victims face risks from both sides of criminal conflicts.
laws.penalty: 10 to 15 years imprisonment; enhanced if worker is killed or seriously injured
exceptions: None — attacks on healthcare workers are always criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Criminal Code — Protection of Healthcare Workers

quiz.q: What specific risk do ambulances face in some areas of Honduras?
options: Being shot at while operating in gang-controlled territory
quiz.explanation: Ambulances and healthcare workers face shooting attacks in gang-controlled territories in Honduras, where criminal organizations view medical personnel as potential informants or threats.

laws.title: Unlicensed Currency Exchange
laws.subtitle: Operating informal money changing without registration
laws.fullDescription: Honduras requires money changers and remittance operators to register with the Central Bank and comply with anti-money laundering regulations. Unregistered currency exchange operations — common at borders and markets — can be used to move criminal proceeds.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years for exchanges facilitating money laundering
exceptions: Individuals exchanging currency for personal travel within permitted amounts

quiz.q: Why must Honduran money changers register with the Central Bank?
options: To pay commissions to the bank
To comply with anti-money laundering regulations
quiz.explanation: Registration of money changers with Honduras Central Bank ensures compliance with anti-money laundering regulations and allows monitoring of currency flows that might represent criminal proceeds.

laws.title: Drug Manufacturing and Processing
laws.subtitle: Operating laboratories to produce illegal drugs
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has been identified as hosting cocaine processing points and methamphetamine production operations. Operating drug manufacturing laboratories carries severe penalties. Law enforcement with DEA cooperation has raided processing facilities in remote rural areas.
laws.penalty: 15 to 25 years imprisonment
exceptions: None

quiz.q: Which international agency cooperates with Honduras in drug lab enforcement?
quiz.explanation: The US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) cooperates directly with Honduras law enforcement to identify and raid drug manufacturing and processing facilities.

laws.title: Illegal Charcoal Production
laws.subtitle: Making charcoal from protected forest wood
laws.fullDescription: Charcoal production drives significant deforestation in Honduras. Producing charcoal from protected forest species without authorization — particularly hardwoods — is prohibited. The practice is economically driven by rural energy poverty but causes irreversible damage to forest cover.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for large-scale operations
exceptions: Authorized charcoal production from non-protected wood species on private land

quiz.q: What economic factor drives illegal charcoal production in Honduras?
options: Rural energy poverty creating cooking fuel demand
quiz.explanation: Rural energy poverty — the inability of poor households to afford cooking fuel alternatives — drives illegal charcoal production from protected forests in Honduras.

laws.title: Targeted Assassination of Activists
laws.subtitle: Killing environmental, indigenous, or labor rights defenders
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has one of the highest rates of killing of environmental and land rights defenders globally. Indigenous activists protecting ancestral lands from mining and dam projects, like Berta Caceres, have been assassinated. The criminal code imposes maximum penalties but impunity remains the norm.
laws.penalty: 30 years imprisonment
exceptions: None

quiz.q: Which famous Honduran activist was assassinated for defending indigenous land rights?
quiz.explanation: Berta Caceres, an indigenous Lenca environmental activist who won the Goldman Environmental Prize for opposing the Agua Zarca dam, was assassinated in 2016 — a case that drew international condemnation.

laws.title: Food Adulteration and Mislabeling
laws.subtitle: Falsifying food ingredients or origin labels
laws.fullDescription: Food adulteration — adding prohibited substances, watering down products, or mislabeling origins and ingredients — is prohibited under Honduras food safety law. The practice defrauds consumers and can cause health harms. ARSA and consumer protection agencies enforce standards.
laws.penalty: Fine; product confiscation; up to 3 years for causing health harm
exceptions: None for knowing adulteration or mislabeling
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Consumer Protection and Food Safety Acts

quiz.q: Which two agencies share responsibility for food labeling enforcement in Honduras?
quiz.explanation: ARSA (food and health safety) and DIACO (consumer protection) share responsibility for enforcing food labeling and adulteration standards in Honduras.

laws.title: Trafficking in Religious Properties
laws.subtitle: Stealing or trafficking sacred indigenous artifacts
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has significant indigenous archaeological and sacred sites. Theft of pre-Columbian artifacts, sacred indigenous objects, and cultural heritage items for international sale is criminalized. Honduras cooperates with international programs to recover stolen cultural property.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 8 years imprisonment; international repatriation obligations
exceptions: None for commercial trafficking in cultural artifacts

quiz.q: What archaeological civilization left major sites in Honduras that require protection?
quiz.explanation: The Maya civilization left significant archaeological sites in Honduras — most notably Copan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site — requiring strong legal protections against looting and artifact trafficking.

laws.title: Cult-Related Crimes
laws.subtitle: Criminal acts committed within extremist religious groups
laws.fullDescription: Honduras law does not prohibit religious belief but criminalizes abuse, fraud, and violence committed within extremist religious contexts. Human sacrifice, unlawful confinement, and financial fraud committed under religious pretexts are prosecuted under applicable criminal law.
laws.penalty: Varies by underlying offense; religious context adds no exemption
exceptions: None — criminal acts receive no exemption for religious motivation
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Criminal Code — No Religious Exemption

quiz.q: Does Honduras law provide religious exemptions for criminal acts committed within religious groups?
options: No — criminal acts receive no religious exemption
quiz.explanation: Honduras law provides no religious exemptions for criminal acts — abuse, fraud, and violence committed within religious contexts are prosecuted under the same criminal law regardless of religious motivation.

laws.title: Unauthorized Tourism in Protected Areas
laws.subtitle: Entering ecological reserves without permits
laws.fullDescription: Honduras national parks and ecological reserves require visitors to enter through official checkpoints with proper permits. Unauthorized access — especially with vehicles or in ecologically sensitive zones — can damage fragile ecosystems. Park rangers enforce access restrictions.
laws.penalty: Fine; removal from protected area
exceptions: Emergency rescue operations and authorized research
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Protected Areas Act — Access Regulations

quiz.q: Why do Honduras protected areas require controlled access through official checkpoints?
options: To prevent damage to fragile ecosystems from unmanaged visitor impact
quiz.explanation: Controlled access to Honduras national parks protects fragile ecosystems from damage caused by unmanaged visitor pressure — vehicles, foot traffic, waste, and noise that can harm biodiversity.

laws.title: Human Organ Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Trading human organs for profit
laws.fullDescription: Trafficking in human organs — including pressuring impoverished people to sell organs or taking organs from trafficking victims — is among the most serious crimes under Honduras law. The law criminalizes all commercial organ transactions outside the official donation system.
laws.penalty: 15 to 25 years imprisonment
exceptions: Official organ donation through authorized transplant programs
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Law Against Human Trafficking — Organ Trade

quiz.q: How does organ trafficking victimize poor populations in Honduras?
options: By pressuring impoverished people to sell organs under economic desperation
quiz.explanation: Organ traffickers exploit extreme poverty in Honduras, pressuring desperate individuals to sell kidneys or other organs for cash — often at a fraction of the value and with inadequate medical follow-up.

laws.title: Insider Trading
laws.subtitle: Trading securities using non-public information
laws.fullDescription: Honduras securities market regulations prohibit insider trading — buying or selling securities based on material non-public information. As Honduras capital market develops, insider trading enforcement is important for maintaining investor confidence and market integrity.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment for significant violations
exceptions: Trades based solely on publicly available information

quiz.q: What harm does insider trading cause to securities markets?
options: It undermines market fairness and investor confidence
quiz.explanation: Insider trading undermines market fairness by allowing privileged traders to profit at the expense of ordinary investors who lack access to the same information — destroying investor confidence.

laws.title: Defamation and False News
laws.subtitle: Publishing false statements that damage reputations
laws.fullDescription: Honduras law criminalizes defamation — making false factual statements that damage a person reputation. The law seeks to balance free expression with protection of reputation. Courts have been criticized for using defamation law against journalists covering government corruption.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment for aggravated cases
exceptions: True statements even if damaging; opinion and commentary clearly labeled
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Criminal Code — Crimes Against Honor

quiz.q: What criticism has been raised about Honduras defamation law enforcement?
options: It has been used against journalists covering government corruption
