quiz.explanation: Honduras defamation laws have been criticized for being used against journalists investigating government corruption — raising concerns that criminal defamation chills legitimate investigative reporting.

laws.title: Cybercrime against Critical Infrastructure
laws.subtitle: Hacking government or utility digital systems
laws.fullDescription: Cyberattacks targeting Honduras government systems, utility networks, and financial infrastructure are criminalized as attacks on critical national security assets. The law imposes enhanced penalties for cybercrimes targeting essential services compared to ordinary computer crimes.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorized government security testing
laws.sourceLabel: Honduras Computer Crimes Act — Critical Infrastructure

quiz.q: Why do attacks on critical infrastructure systems carry enhanced penalties in Honduras?
options: Essential services disruption affects millions of people
quiz.explanation: Cyberattacks on Honduras critical infrastructure — government systems, utilities, financial networks — carry enhanced penalties because their disruption can affect millions of people who depend on essential services.

laws.title: Union Busting and Anti-Labor Retaliation
laws.subtitle: Illegally preventing workers from organizing
laws.fullDescription: Honduras labor code protects the right of workers to organize unions and engage in collective bargaining. Employers who illegally fire union organizers, threaten workers for union activity, or take other retaliatory action face both administrative penalties and criminal prosecution.
laws.penalty: Fine; reinstatement orders; up to 2 years imprisonment for serious violations
exceptions: Legitimate dismissals unrelated to union activity following due process

quiz.q: What worker right does Honduras labor code protect that employers cannot legally obstruct?
options: The right to refuse all work
The right to organize unions and engage in collective bargaining
quiz.explanation: Honduras labor code protects workers right to organize unions and engage in collective bargaining — and criminalizes employer retaliation against workers exercising these protected rights.

laws.title: Incitement to Ethnic Violence
laws.subtitle: Promoting violence against indigenous or ethnic groups
laws.fullDescription: Honduras has significant indigenous populations including Lenca, Garifuna, Maya-Chorti, and Miskito peoples. Inciting violence or hatred against these groups is criminalized under Honduras hate crime provisions, reflecting the country diverse ethnic composition.
laws.penalty: 5 to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Academic research and good-faith historical discussion

quiz.q: Which indigenous groups are protected by Honduras hate crime provisions?
options: Lenca, Garifuna, Maya-Chorti, and Miskito among others
quiz.explanation: Honduras hate crime provisions protect diverse indigenous peoples including the Lenca, Garifuna, Maya-Chorti, and Miskito — reflecting the country multicultural indigenous heritage.

laws.title: Illegal Arms Importation
laws.subtitle: Smuggling military weapons into Honduras
laws.fullDescription: Honduras is a target for illegal arms trafficking that supplies criminal gangs with weapons exceeding civilian legal limits. Military-grade weapons — machine guns, rocket launchers, and large-caliber rifles — are smuggled from the United States, Central America, and elsewhere. Strict penalties target the supply chains arming Honduran violence.
laws.penalty: 15 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorized military and police procurement through official channels

quiz.q: From where do many illegal weapons reach Honduras criminal networks?
options: United States, Central America, and other smuggling sources
quiz.explanation: Illegal weapons in Honduras arrive through smuggling routes originating in the United States, Central America, and other sources — supplying criminal gangs with military-grade arms that fuel gang violence.
